**Last checked:** 2026-11-13, against `master` at `65ddaf5` in
`Symplectomorphism/c-gnn`. The full records are in the discussion
compendium (`reports/supporting_docs/discussion-compendium/`).

## Open

::: {.callout-important collapse="true"}
## Finding the indirect lift routinely (open; the target)
The indirect lift, held at every instant, is the paper's running chain; its
last four edits and closing transport are certified over μ ∈ [0.3, 0.5].
From the scene alone, the planner finds the held indirect lift in 33 of 34
held-out searches with V₁ and π of round 1 (192 calls each; mean 86 calls to a
solve), in the current configuration: admissible transition poses, δ-eroded
transport targets, the box's rotation over ±180°
([Results](../results/index.qmd)). The one failure (seed 11, start 8,
μ = 0.5) runs out of actions to try after 125 calls. V₀ alone is not
re-measured in this configuration; in the previous one (±90° stop, no
erosion) it solved 17 of 34 and V₁ + π 26. Open: the remaining failure; the
short searches (in the previous configuration none of 18 solved with 64 calls:
the roll from the tilts first reached is refused); and the next rounds of V₁ and π (training searches that reach the
goal, exploration).
Given the formation sequence as a hint, the same planner solves only at
μ = 0.5: the hint removes the other routes.
:::

::: {.callout-important collapse="true"}
## Near-future: the disk's motion keeps the box held; pushes aimed inside their targets
**1. The disk's motion keeps the box held (#23).** Every disk motion, the
approach included, must keep the box held under the gate's test, including
the disk's own contact force. The diagnosed fall had a transition pose 16 mm
inside the box: the approach drove the disk's reference into it and the
disk's PD pressed harder and harder. Part 1 is on by default: transition
poses must be admissible, so no disk target is buried in the box. On the 34
held-out searches falls drop by 17–23% and the solves are unchanged. Part B
is built and measured: the approach covers the whole run to its target, the
hold test runs along that path with the disk's predicted force as an external
load, and a failing approach is refused before anything moves. On the 34
held-out searches it solves the same 33 with the same calls; its 27 refusals
fall where the box would have fallen (22 of the 25 that can be compared). Whether
it becomes the default is open.

**2. Pushes aimed inside their targets (#24).** The failing searches did not
need the disk re-placed on its face; its height plays no part. They end in a
dead band about 23–35 mm from the riser, where neither make(s) nor a push is
offered: a push counted as reaching its target when it ended within δ of the
target set's far edge. Fixed by the **δ-erosion of transport targets**, on by
default: pushes aim inside the target set by δ. Measured on the 34 held-out
searches in the previous configuration: V₀ 17 → 26 of 34, V₁+π 26 → 33 of 34.
Under the current configuration V₁+π solves 33 of 34
([Results](../results/index.qmd)).

**3. A dynamic realizer (#34).** The architecture is adopted: a certified
tube per edit carries the claim and a fixed-mode MPC tracks inside it.
[The dynamic realizer](dynamic-realizer.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-important collapse="true"}
## The realizer plans held poses, not stick–slip plans
Λ<sub>qs</sub> plans positions only and models forces as the gate's hold test
at each knot (both edges of every cone): a sequence of static holds, Theorem
B's level. With its two path fixes (`disk_path_fix`, `roll_press_fix`, on by
default) the unhinted search finds the indirect lift ([Results](../results/index.qmd)).
The gate stays at the hold level. A stick–slip variant of the realizer is
built (`stick_slip`, off): it realizes 9–12 fewer of 227 replayed calls per μ
and its chain search fails at 0.3, so it stays off.
[The local solver](local-solver.qmd#qs-slip). No executed motion is
certified: Λ<sub>qs</sub> tracks within 8.1° and 17 mm at 95/95, against a
certificate resolution of 0.25° × 0.5 mm. The replacement, a realizer that
plans the motion with its contact dynamics, is on
[The dynamic realizer](dynamic-realizer.qmd).
:::

::: {.callout-important collapse="true"}
## The open work, in order
1. **Discovery.** Rebuild 𝒱₀ for the current gate; train V₁ by expert
   iteration with exploration (π mixing, Go-Explore restarts), with a
   certified Lipschitz bound before V₁ decides acceptance; then the attention
   ranker, trained on held solves.
2. **A value that only orders** (H4): lexicographic value, edge lengths from
   measured calls, the η<sub>max</sub> sweep; a derived replacement for the
   progress threshold δ = 10 mm, which rests on the declared merge radius.
3. **Parametric certificate of the support LP.** Certify a hold along a whole
   path, not at sampled poses: the transport gate (it replaces the five-pose
   check), the lazy target query (an exclusion certificate) and the realizer
   (held between plan knots). Queued with it: a polynomial (sum-of-squares)
   certificate for large regions and an online tube certificate of the next
   segment of Λ<sub>qs</sub>'s plan.
4. **Certified execution**: [the dynamic realizer](dynamic-realizer.qmd)
   (the A-tracker, then the B-tube, then the A3 check), with H2's items:
   plan knots held throughout, admissible end knots, a tracking bound, the
   free-approach window; the pushes that stop 3–5 mm short (`slide_lag`
   stays until then).
5. **H3, a judge that measures "held"**: the hold margin along the trajectory
   instead of the 6 mm kinetic-energy threshold for dynamic events.
6. **A3, the uncertainty model**: ε by a 95/95 bound, the μ band's
   robustness, ε<sub>pen</sub>.
7. **Gate decisions (Aykut)**: the target threshold (R4); when an edit must
   close locally; the lazy query's exclusion certificate; a gate whose
   necessity needs no Lipschitz or covering hypothesis (refuse only where the
   interval certificate proves "not held"); the recognizer rethink.
8. **Releases R1–R3**: let go only at a held node, the physically possible
   outcomes, a statistical release certificate. A proposal; releases are off
   until then.
9. **Scenes**: a taller step (H = a/2), the scene families, then a second
   disk.
10. **Housekeeping**: JAX loops (the gate takes 20–35 s per call on GPU);
    the clusters' memory-map limit (below).
:::

[]{#eps-pen}

::: {.callout-warning collapse="true"}
## Ties under deep overlap (ε<sub>pen</sub> = 5 mm is provisional)
ε<sub>pen</sub> is ten times ε<sub>on</sub>, so both corners of a tilted box
edge can count as touching. 257 of 4,000 demo poses jittered by about 3 mm
are ambiguous at 5 mm (475 at 10 mm; in many, s<sub>v</sub> loses to t,
which contains it). A tied pose is never a search node or a solver success,
so no wrong label is used. 2–3 mm (44–98 ties) needs stiffer contacts, which
keep penetration under 0.22 mm but need the controller retuned first.
[Contact states](contact-states.qmd#the-recognizer).
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Smaller open items
- **Lift searches exceed the clusters' memory-map limit (#27)** of 65,530
  maps per process. One cut leaves results bit-identical and lowers the peak
  from about 100k to 79k maps, still above the limit; an HPC ticket to raise
  the limit is open.
- **Label flicker near θ<sub>e</sub>** along a trajectory. Fix: hysteresis
  with thresholds from a noise model, in the execution monitor.
- **GPU runs are not repeatable between processes** by default. Workaround:
  `XLA_FLAGS=--xla_gpu_deterministic_ops=true`, about 13% slower.
- **3D is frozen.** The 3D hold LP needs reinversion (float32 rounding in
  linrax's dense tableau leaves about 1% of supported 3D cases "uncertain",
  never certified wrongly), and the 3D catalog (`step.yaml`) keeps its old
  defects. The project is planar.
- **`ContactGraph` drops edges** (`self.edges` never set). Nothing uses the
  graph.
- **`tests/test_local_solver.py`** reads `gradient_warm_start`, which MPPI no
  longer has. For a fix-up PR to Angelo.
:::

## Decisions behind the current design

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## Settled: the stuttering motion, replays across processors, the box's rotation range
- **The stuttering motion (#25, closed).** The renderer's playback is fixed:
  one continuous timeline, with no frozen holds between calls. The chatter
  during the pivot is a MuJoCo sliding-contact artifact: above a slip speed
  v\*(N) a loaded sliding contact floats to zero penetration, drops out for a
  step and the box bounces. v\* is calibrated per contact pair, and its slope
  follows from the contact parameters (`solref`, `solimp`). Timing the plan
  below v\* needs a Coulomb force solution, and Λ<sub>qs</sub>'s hand-built
  disk path has none on the steep pivots, so the fix moves to
  [the dynamic realizer](dynamic-realizer.qmd), which chooses the disk's path
  with its forces.
- **Replays across processors (#28, closed).** Every run records its build
  (processor, instruction set, libraries, XLA settings) and its code commit.
  A replay on the same build must reproduce the run bit for bit; on another
  processor the difference is reported, not judged. Measured on 80 stratified
  calls: 80 of 80 bit-identical on one machine, 0 of 80 across a Ryzen and an
  i5, and 2 of 80 flip between success and failure.
- **The box's rotation range is ±180°.** The rotation joint was limited to
  ±90°, and that stop acted as a hidden support; it is relaxed to ±180°.
:::

::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"}
## The construction, the gate, the realizer and the search
- **Xiao and Ji's contact formations, exactly**, with tolerances, several
  bodies with a manipulator, and a no-contact state per pair: principal
  contacts, transfers by one-sided containment, compound edges by the
  minimality rule, the environment one polygon whose convex vertices come
  from its geometry. Simpler representations (stances, body-pair strata,
  scene graphs) cannot see a box tip from its edge onto its corner.
  [Contact states](contact-states.qmd), [edits](edits.qmd).
- **The landed box is {t}**: landing is transfer(s<sub>v</sub> → t), and
  sliding off the corner is transport. [Edits](edits.qmd#the-step-chain).
- **One derived edge-contact tilt**, θ<sub>e</sub> = arcsin(ε<sub>on</sub>/h),
  shared by the floor and riser contacts. [Contact states](contact-states.qmd).
- **Validity from the geometry** (a certified table of valid formations) and
  the **local compound rule** (ρ = 25 mm).
  [Contact states](contact-states.qmd#validity), [edits](edits.qmd).
- **The gate tests the edit's less-constrained end**, with the disk's motor
  limits, and its margin is a **certified bound**: "held" needs a witness,
  "not held" a Farkas certificate, else uncertain. It certifies holds only;
  stick or slip belongs to the realizer's plan. [The hold gate](hold-gate.qmd).
- **The transition sweep** uses a canonical basis of the free directions and
  an adaptive grid (64 poses, two refinement levels); makes and constraining
  transfers close the added contact. [The hold gate](hold-gate.qmd#sweep).
- **Disk friction is a declared band**, μ<sub>disk</sub> ∈ [0.3, 0.5], one
  model everywhere; the gate and the tracker use 0.3.
- **The gate is relaxed over the disk's region**, and nodes are keyed by
  formation, disk region and box pose, merged only when the gate's verdicts
  agree, with the safe duplicate rule. [Node identity](node-identity.qmd).
- **One success test for every realizer.** [The local solver](local-solver.qmd).
- **Λ<sub>qs</sub>'s feed-forward is the minimum-norm holding force**, and
  its six options are on by default.
  [The local solver](local-solver.qmd#lambda-qs-options).
- **Releases and the learned skills are in the code, off**: the method's lift
  is held at every instant, and no edit of it needs a learned skill.
  [The local solver](local-solver.qmd#learned-skill), [search](search.qmd#design).
:::
